source_anchor: Kant Critique of Pure Reason A6-10/B10-14; Prolegomena §2
instance: Kant distinguishes a priori from a posteriori knowledge and analytic from synthetic propositions, yielding four combinations. State why synthetic a priori is the philosophically important category and give one mathematical proposition Kant claims is synthetic a priori. Note one reason a 21st-century reader may disagree.

answer_features.claim: synthetic a priori is a third source of knowledge beyond pure logic and pure observation
example: 7+5=12 (or similar arithmetic) treated as synthetic a priori
Frege/Russell logicism would reduce arithmetic to logic, making it analytic

candidate_responses.text: Synthetic a priori would be a third knowledge source beyond logic and observation. Kant says 7+5=12 is one. A modern reader may disagree because Frege and Russell reduce arithmetic to logic, making it analytic.
It is the category that is informative AND independent of experience. 7+5=12. But logicism challenges that.
